Rules / Correctness

SK2012 Review a self-operation on an automatic property

The same known automatic property is used on both sides of an assignment or built-in comparison.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

The compiler already reports many field/local self-operations but leaves property spellings unchecked. Arbitrary getters or setters can have deliberate behavior, so this rule requires a non-virtual source auto-property and a stable identical receiver. A report asks for review rather than deleting an operation or inventing the intended target.

Example

Instead of:

int Value { get; set; } void M() { Value = Value; }

Write:

int Value { get; set; } void M(int value) { Value = value; }

When it does not fire

Only ordinary, non-virtual, non-override, non-abstract, non-partial auto-properties declared in the same source file are supported; another file's accessor body is not a per-file cache fact. Indexers, custom accessors, ref returns, explicit interface properties, unstable receivers and compiler-covered CS1717/CS1718 cases are excluded. Comparisons are restricted to non-lifted integral/char, bool, enum and string operations; floating-point NaN tests and custom equality are not reported. No automatic fix is offered; intentional synchronization or external weaving can require suppression.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK2012.severity
